newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-BHP says Griffin still shut-in.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-BHP says Griffin still shut-in.

text.p: The Griffin oil field offshore Western Australia was still shut-in late on Friday afternoon, a The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd (BHP) spokesman said.

Earlier on Friday BHP had expected that Griffin might be able to resume pumping crude late Friday but the spokesman said from Perth that BHP was still watching and waiting to see how a nearby tropical low develops.
Production was halted on Thursday because of the tropical depression which Australia's Meteorology Bureau said earlier on Friday could develop into a tropical cyclone.
The spokesman said the low appears to be stationary at the moment about 183 nautical miles northwest of Griffin.
The Griffin riser is still connected and BHP will wait to see if the low develops into a cyclone before disconnecting and sailing the floating storage vessel out of the storm's way, he said.
"It's just a monitoring exercise at the moment," he said.
He said it was not possible to say when it was likely production could resume.
Griffin produces at the rate of about 80,000 barrels per day (bpd).

Equal-stake partners in the North West Shelf, where the Cossack Pioneer field is situated, are units of BHP, The British Petroleum Co Plc, Japan Australia LNG (MiMi) Pty Ltd -- a partnership of Mitsui & Co Ltd and Mitsubishi Corp -- Chevron Corp, the Royal Dutch/Shell Group and Woodside.
